1 Syntax: the model

no sample for cut: reads the
manual and --help; three
syntaxes, one per selector;
copies uniq's '=' marker onto
-b, -c, -f, -d; misses that -d
and -s need -f
2 Choose what to run: model

21 runs by hand (call 13):
ranges, long forms with '=',
errors (two selectors, none,
2-char -d, -b0); never -d or -s
with -b/-c; 4 of 17 spellings
never run
3 Run and observe: model

plain shell in /tmp, on a
three-line file; reads what
cut prints and its exit code;
no strace (not needed for
a command that only reads)
4 Decide behaviour: model

reasons that each line is
independent, then tests it after
writing: 5,000 lines, 4 chunks,
join = one run (5 option sets);
round robin equal as a multiset
5 Write PaSh's form: model

table = PaSh's own minus -M
(which GNU cut rejects); classes
match PaSh's, except no split
under -z; checked only against
stand-ins that accept anything

Scale for cut. v1's generator, at its shipped limit of 4 flags, writes 75,172 command lines from its reference grammar, 11,651 of them distinct (measured here); cut accepts 1,783,
of which 360 do real work (the rest carry --help or --version). The agent ran cut 21 times before writing and 45 times after, all hand-chosen.

v1 is shown as the paper designs it (sections 2-6), not as run for this comparison. Counts marked 'measured here' come from v1's own generator and GNU coreutils 9.4 in the pash VM. Method, not quality, is compared.
